{{short description|Relates abstract sheaf cohomology with Čech cohomology}}
In [[algebraic topology]] and [[algebraic geometry]], '''Leray's theorem''' (so named after [[Jean Leray]]) relates abstract [[sheaf cohomology]] with [[Čech cohomology]].

Let <math>\mathcal{F}</math> be a sheaf on a [[topological space]] <math>X</math> and <math>\mathcal{U} = \{U_i\}_{i \in I}</math> an [[open cover]] of <math>X</math>. If <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is acyclic on every finite intersection of elements of <math>\mathcal{U}</math> (meaning that <math>H^k(U_{i_0} \cap \dots \cap U_{i_n}, \mathcal{F}) = 0</math> for all <math>k \geq 1</math> and all finite intersections <math>U_{i_0} \cap \dots \cap U_{i_n}</math>), then there is an isomorphism

<math>\check{H}^q(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) \cong H^q(X, \mathcal{F})</math>

for all <math>q \geq 0</math>, where <math>\check{H}^q(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})</math> is the <math>q</math>-th [[Čech cohomology]] group of <math>\mathcal{F}</math> with respect to the open cover <math>\mathcal{U}</math>, and <math>H^q(X, \mathcal{F})</math> is the abstract [[sheaf cohomology]] group.

== Proof ==
The standard modern proof of Leray's theorem relies on [[Spectral sequence|spectral sequences]], specifically the Čech-to-derived functor spectral sequence.

Let <math>\mathcal{F}</math> be a sheaf on <math>X</math> and <math>\mathcal{U}</math> an open cover. There exists a spectral sequence relating [[Čech cohomology]] to abstract [[sheaf cohomology]], whose second page is given by:

<math>E_2^{p,q} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{H}^q(\mathcal{F})) \Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X, \mathcal{F})</math>

where <math>\mathcal{H}^q(\mathcal{F})</math> denotes the [[presheaf]] defined by <math>V \mapsto H^q(V, \mathcal{F})</math>.

The acyclicity hypothesis states that for any finite intersection <math>V = U_{i_0} \cap \dots \cap U_{i_p}</math> of sets in <math>\mathcal{U}</math>, we have <math>H^q(V, \mathcal{F}) = 0</math> for all <math>q \geq 1</math>. Consequently, the presheaf <math>\mathcal{H}^q(\mathcal{F})</math> evaluates to <math>0</math> on all finite intersections of the cover.

This implies that the Čech complex computing <math>\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))</math> is identically zero for <math>q \geq 1</math>. Therefore, the spectral sequence degenerates at the <math>E_2</math> page:

<math>E_2^{p,q} = 0 \quad \text{for } q > 0</math>

Because the spectral sequence degenerates, the terms on the <math>p</math>-axis of the second page are isomorphic to the target of the spectral sequence:

<math>E_2^{p,0} \cong H^p(X, \mathcal{F})</math>

For <math>q = 0</math>, the presheaf <math>\mathcal{H}^0(\mathcal{F})</math> assigns to each open set <math>V</math> the module of sections <math>H^0(V, \mathcal{F}) = \mathcal{F}(V)</math>. Thus, <math>\mathcal{H}^0(\mathcal{F})</math> is exactly the sheaf <math>\mathcal{F}</math> itself, which means <math>E_2^{p,0} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})</math>. This collapse yields the desired isomorphism:

<math>\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) \cong H^p(X, \mathcal{F})</math>
